lessons.title: Prepositions of Time: in, on, at
lessons.content:
We use IN, ON and AT to say when something happens.

AT is for exact times and some expressions:
• at 7 o'clock, at midnight, at noon
• at the weekend (British English), at night, at Christmas

ON is for days and dates:
• on Monday, on Friday morning
• on 25 December, on my birthday

IN is for longer periods:
• in the morning / afternoon / evening
• in July, in winter, in 2024
• in the 21st century

Tip: small → AT (a time), medium → ON (a day), big → IN (months, years, seasons).

questions.prompt: The film starts ___ 8 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Use AT for exact clock times.

questions.prompt: My birthday is ___ June.
We have English ___ Tuesday.
questions.explanation: Use ON for days of the week.

questions.prompt: I usually read a book ___ the evening.
The shops are closed ___ Christmas Day.
questions.explanation: Christmas DAY is a specific day, so ON. (But: at Christmas = the holiday period.)

questions.prompt: “In 1998” is correct.
“On night” is correct.

lessons.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
lessons.content:
PRESENT SIMPLE (I work, she works)
Use it for habits, routines and facts.
• I get up at 7 every day.
• Water boils at 100°C.
• She doesn't like coffee.
Signal words: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day.
Remember: he/she/it + -s → he plays, she watches, it goes.

PRESENT CONTINUOUS (I am working, she is working)
Use it for actions happening now or around now, and temporary situations.
• Look! It's raining.
• I'm studying for my exams this week.
• They aren't watching TV at the moment.
Signal words: now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen!, today, this week.

Stative verbs (like, love, know, want, believe, understand) are not usually used in the continuous form:
✓ I know the answer.  ✗ I am knowing the answer.

questions.prompt: Listen! The baby ___.
questions.explanation: “Listen!” shows it is happening now → present continuous.

questions.prompt: My father ___ to work by bus every day.
questions.explanation: “Every day” is a routine → present simple, he + goes.

questions.prompt: I ___ what you mean.
questions.explanation: “Understand” is a stative verb, so present simple.

questions.prompt: She ___ (not / like) spicy food.
questions.explanation: Negative present simple with she: doesn't + base verb.

questions.prompt: Please be quiet. I ___ (study) right now.
“Water is boiling at 100°C” is the best way to state this scientific fact.
questions.explanation: Facts use the present simple: Water boils at 100°C.

questions.prompt: What ___ this weekend?
questions.explanation: Plans and arrangements for the near future often use the present continuous.

lessons.title: Past Simple: Regular and Irregular Verbs
lessons.content:
We use the PAST SIMPLE for finished actions in the past, often with a time: yesterday, last week, in 2010, two days ago.

Regular verbs add -ed:
• work → worked, play → played
• live → lived (verb ends in -e: add -d)
• stop → stopped (short verb: double the consonant)
• study → studied (consonant + y → -ied)

Irregular verbs have special forms you must learn:
• go → went, have → had, see → saw, buy → bought
• eat → ate, take → took, write → wrote, be → was/were

Negatives and questions use DID + base verb:
• I didn't go to school yesterday. (NOT: I didn't went)
• Did you see the match?

questions.prompt: Yesterday I ___ (go) to the cinema with my friends.
They ___ (study) all night for the test.
We ___ a great film last night.
questions.explanation: See → saw (past simple). “Seen” is the past participle.

questions.prompt: She didn't ___ breakfast this morning.
questions.explanation: After didn't use the base verb.

questions.prompt: ___ you buy a new phone last week?
questions.explanation: Questions in the past simple use Did + base verb.

questions.prompt: The past simple of “stop” is “stoped”.
My grandmother ___ (write) me a letter last month.

lessons.title: Comparatives and Superlatives
lessons.content:
Use COMPARATIVES to compare two things, and SUPERLATIVES to say something is the most in a group.

Short adjectives (one syllable): add -er / -est
• tall → taller → the tallest
• big → bigger → the biggest (double the consonant)

Adjectives ending in -y: change y to -ier / -iest
• happy → happier → the happiest

Long adjectives (two or more syllables): more / the most
• expensive → more expensive → the most expensive
• interesting → more interesting → the most interesting

Irregular:
• good → better → the best
• bad → worse → the worst
• far → further/farther → the furthest/farthest

Use THAN after a comparative: My brother is taller than me.
Use THE before a superlative: It's the best day of my life.

questions.prompt: An elephant is ___ than a horse.
questions.explanation: Comparing two things → comparative; double the g.

questions.prompt: This is ___ book I have ever read.
Today is ___ (good) than yesterday.
She is the ___ (happy) person I know.
“More cheap” is the correct comparative of “cheap”.
My test result was ___ than yours.

lessons.title: Reading: A Saturday at the Market
lessons.content:
Every Saturday morning, Amina goes to the market with her grandfather. They leave the house at half past seven because the best fruit is sold early.

Her grandfather always buys the same things: oranges, fresh bread and a small bag of olives. Amina likes to look at the colourful spices, but she doesn't like the fish section because of the smell.

Last Saturday was different. It was raining heavily, so there were not many people at the market. The orange seller, Mr Karim, was happy to see them. He gave Amina a free apple and told her a funny story about his donkey.

On the way home, Amina's grandfather said, “Rainy days are the best days for the market. The sellers have more time to talk.” Amina agreed. She thinks the market is more interesting than the supermarket because every visit is a little adventure.

questions.prompt: Why do Amina and her grandfather leave early?
options: Because the best fruit is sold early
questions.explanation: “They leave … because the best fruit is sold early.”

questions.prompt: Amina enjoys the fish section.
questions.explanation: She doesn't like the fish section because of the smell.

questions.prompt: What did Mr Karim give Amina?
Last Saturday there were not many people because it was ___.
questions.explanation: “It was raining heavily, so there were not many people.”

questions.prompt: Amina's grandfather thinks rainy days are good for the market.
questions.explanation: “Rainy days are the best days for the market.”

questions.prompt: Why does Amina prefer the market to the supermarket?
options: Every visit is a little adventure
It is closer to her house

questions.prompt: In the text, the word “heavily” means…

lessons.title: Everyday Phrasal Verbs
lessons.content:
A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (up, on, after, out…). The meaning is often different from the verb alone.

• look after = take care of — She looks after her little brother.
• look for = try to find — I'm looking for my keys.
• give up = stop doing something — He gave up smoking last year.
• get up = leave your bed — I get up at 6:30.
• turn on / turn off = start / stop a machine — Turn off the lights, please.
• find out = discover information — I found out the truth.
• run out of = have no more — We've run out of milk.
• put on = dress yourself in — Put on your coat; it's cold.

questions.prompt: Can you ___ my cat while I'm on holiday?
I can't find my phone. Can you help me ___ it?
Don't ___ up! You can do it.
We've run ___ of sugar. Can you buy some?
questions.explanation: Run out of = have no more.

questions.prompt: “Find out” means “to discover information”.
It's cold. ___ your jacket.
questions.explanation: Put on = dress yourself in clothes.

questions.prompt: Please turn ___ the TV before you go to bed.
